releases.body:
### Minor Changes

- 5f97b7e: feat: opt-in pre-deployment dogfood gate (Policy 27)

    Gates PR creation on a recorded run of the change on real hardware. Off by
    default, so no existing repository changes behavior.

    - `record_dogfood` records a run as `dogfood` evidence bound to the workspace,
      commit hash, and tracked-content worktree fingerprint. A tracked edit or new
      commit after the run makes the evidence stale.
    - Only a `pass` is durable, and only the newest record per workspace and host
      is kept. A `hold` stays diagnosable in memory with its taxonomy class and
      never becomes evidence. Recording a `hold` also discards that host's cached
      passes, so a process restart cannot re-open the gate on an older green run.
    - A `pass` requires every check row to be `pass` and at least one check row
      to exist, so the gate cannot be satisfied by a skipped check or by an empty
      observation. A `hold` must name a taxonomy class.
    - `requireDogfood` and `dogfoodDeployMatrix` (or `WORKFLOW_GUARD_REQUIRE_DOGFOOD`
      and `WORKFLOW_GUARD_DOGFOOD_DEPLOY_MATRIX`) enable the gate and declare the
      host labels that each need a passing run. Retention and hold eviction are per
      host and scoped to the workspace, so repeated runs in one repository or on one
      host cannot evict another repository's or host's only pass.
    - `WORKFLOW_GUARD_DOGFOOD_ACTOR`/`WORKFLOW_GUARD_DOGFOOD_DEPTH` mark a session
      spawned by a repository runner. Every policy still applies there, and the
      marker only refuses `record_dogfood`, so a tested session cannot certify
      itself.
    - `guard_status` reports `lastDogfood` and adds `dogfood` to
      `outstandingRequirements` when the gate is unsatisfied.

### Patch Changes

- c983c70: Report a verification timeout as a timeout, not as a failing test.

    Finalization runs the verify command with a bounded timeout. When the command
    exceeded it, the guard killed the process tree and then reported the outcome
    with the same message it uses for a failing assertion: "all tasks marked done
    but verification is failing". That wording sent the agent looking for a test
    that failed. Nothing had failed; the suite never finished, so the result was
    unknown.

    The two conditions now carry separate codes and reasons. `runVerify` returns
    `timedOut` and the limit that was hit, and the dispatcher emits
    `verification_timed_out` with a message naming the elapsed limit and the remedy
    (`verifyTimeoutMs` in `.opencode/workflow-guard.json`, or
    `WORKFLOW_GUARD_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_MS`). A genuine failure keeps
    `verification_failed` and its output tail unchanged.

    Both still block finalization. A timeout is not evidence of passing work, so
    allowing it through would be a silent weakening of the verification gate. Only
    the attribution changed.

    Regression coverage asserts five things: a timeout blocks finalization, the
    block reason does not claim a failure, the snipped tail carries no "Verification
    Failed" header, the limit is named at the precision it was set, and the reason
    names a remedy. Four of those fail against the previous message; the block
    itself already held, and must keep holding.

    The remedy is the one lever the agent cannot pull. `.opencode/workflow-guard.json`
    is tamper-protected, so the reason names both the project setting and the
    environment variable, and the operator applies it. That is deliberate: the guard
    reports what it knows, and does not pretend the agent can widen its own gate.

### Minor Changes

- 2a68c41: Qualify against OpenCode 2.2.0.

    OpenCode 2.2.0 reorganizes the `@opencode/ai` export surface. `Message` is no
    longer reachable from the package root there, and a root named import throws
    `SyntaxError: The requested module '@opencode/ai' does not provide an export
named 'Message'`. A V2 plugin that cannot be evaluated registers no hooks, so
    every policy would be inert while the host looks healthy. This release moves the
    import and the pins to the 2.2.0 package set.

    - **Import path.** `Message` moves from the `@opencode/ai` root to
      `@opencode/ai/effect`. On 2.2.0 the root no longer re-exports the schema
      surface, so a root named import throws, as quoted above; verified against the
      installed 2.2.0 dist. `@opencode/plugin@2.2.0` itself imports `Message` from
      `/effect`, so this is the host's own sanctioned path. No call site changes:
      `Message.user` is still the constructor used at `src/lib/v2-plugin.ts:542`.
    - **Pins.** `@opencode/plugin` and `@opencode/ai` move to `2.2.0`, and
      `@opentui/solid` to `0.7.0`, which `@opencode/plugin@2.2.0` declares as an
      exact peer requirement. `@opentui/core` is deliberately not added as a direct
      dependency: `@opentui/solid@0.7.0` already declares it as an exact dependency,
      so an extra pin would duplicate a resolution the tree already settles. The
      `@opencode-ai/plugin` `1.19.3` V1 pin is unchanged. Of the existing `overrides`
      entries, `solid-js` `1.9.17` still applies because `@opentui/solid@0.7.0` still
      peer-pins exactly `1.9.12`; `toml` `5.0.1` is unaffected.
    - **Todo capability.** The registry probe already covers this host, so 2.2.0
      needs no version check. Verified on the live 2.2.0 binary: `available` with
      `experimental.todo: true`, `unavailable` without it.
    - **Docs.** `docs/installation.md` carries a 1.18.x / 2.2.0 qualification row
      listing only the seats actually exercised, and the pin-set paragraph now
      explains the `@opencode/ai` root-versus-`/effect` boundary and why
      `@opentui/core` needs no direct pin.
    - **Test coverage.** `test/test-e2e.mts` gains two canaries that need no model
      provider: the permission seat denies a real finding and abstains on an
      undecidable push. They run inside the real host setup with the workspace taken
      from the host's own `location.directory`; the push case passes no client,
      because the point is that simulation skips the remote PR probe. The deny
      canary asserts policy identity (`secrets` / `secret_read`), not message prose.

    Verified on OpenCode v2.2.0: `npm run typecheck` clean, `npm test` 1370 passed /
    0 failed, `npm run test:install` 32 passed / 0 failed. The opt-in model-driven
    probes remained unavailable because the provider returned
    `Model unavailable` before guard behavior could run, which that harness reports
    as `live unavailable` rather than as a guard failure.

    The `zod` advisory is also cleared here. `GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5` covers
    `zod <4.6.6`, and the vulnerable `4.1.8` copy arrived through the exact
    `@opencode-ai/plugin@1.19.3` V1 pin while the V2 entrypoint imports `zod`
    without declaring it. A new `zod: 4.6.6` override dedupes both onto one patched
    copy, and `npm audit` now reports zero vulnerabilities. That override must be
    applied with a clean reinstall: an incremental `npm install` leaves the old
    resolution in place and fails 14 `test:install` checks, which reads as an
    incompatibility but is a stale tree.

    One pre-existing issue is deliberately not fixed here, because it needs a real
    binary probe and changes behavior beyond a host qualification:
    `src/lib/policy-posture.ts` describes the `code-mode-surface` rule as inert on the
    qualified hosts because they "register no `execute` tool". That rationale is not
    accurate: the tool is registered, and this repository's own session calls

### Minor Changes

- 495ba8a: Add Policy 25, the live-documentation research floor. After repeated tool failures (default 3) with no live-documentation lookup since, the guard blocks the next mutation or shell call and directs the agent to consult a current source (`websearch`/`webfetch`, or an MCP documentation tool) instead of guessing from training data. Reads, greps, and research tools are never blocked.

    The floor is debt-based rather than success-based: an unrelated successful tool does not clear the debt, so a benign command cannot slip a guessed change back through. Only a successful research call clears it. It is enabled by default to force the failover and can be disabled with `requireLiveDocs: false` / `WORKFLOW_GUARD_REQUIRE_LIVE_DOCS=0`, or retuned with `liveDocFailureThreshold` / `WORKFLOW_GUARD_LIVE_DOC_THRESHOLD`. Decisions are audited (`reason: live_docs_research_floor`) and block feedback flows to the app log at warn level.

    Note for operators: the acting agent must be permitted to call a research tool, or the floor will (correctly) stall it. Agents whose toolset denies `websearch`/`webfetch` and exposes no MCP docs server should be granted one. Both the V1 and V2 entrypoints enforce the floor in parity.

    The gated surface is every mutating call, not just edits and shell: it includes `guard_worktree_create`, `guard_worktree_cleanup`, and `guard_recovery_restore`, so a guard-provided tool cannot be the way past a guard gate. Research recognition matches documented MCP server names (`mcp__context7__*`, `mcp__deepwiki__*`, `mcp__tavily__*`, `mcp__brave__*`), so a guard inspection tool or generic file reader cannot clear the debt by name accident. An unrecognised docs server can be declared with `researchTools` / `WORKFLOW_GUARD_RESEARCH_TOOLS`. A failed research attempt never accrues debt, so a flaky network cannot deepen the block it was meant to clear. An unparseable or non-positive threshold falls back to the default of 3 instead of silently disabling the floor.

    Also add Policy 26, sweeping repository claims vs read coverage. It is observability-only (like Policy 24): when the final response asserts a whole-repository fact ("the entire codebase uses X", "no other callers reference this") but the session has read or authored fewer than 2 distinct files, the mismatch is journaled and logged at info level. The response is never blocked or rewritten, since a search-heavy investigation can legitimately back such a claim with little read coverage. Both entrypoints report it in parity.

### Minor Changes

- e5fd6a1: Enforce per-task completion evidence for `todowrite`.

    A task may now enter `completed` only when the session recorded at least one file mutation inside that task's active window. Previously, a list-wide `todowrite` could flip every item to `completed` with no work behind it; the guard only journalled a `completion_claim_mismatch` audit record and allowed it. That signal is now an enforced policy.

    - **Per-task windows, not a session baseline.** Each active task records the session mutation count when it entered its current window. One mutation cannot vouch for several completions, so N completions need N mutations counted from the earliest of them, and work done before a task became active never counts toward it. A finished or dropped task releases its window, so reusing a task's text starts clean. Task identity is the task text with the read-only marker stripped, and occurrences are counted rather than matched by last write, so duplicate text cannot hide a new completion.
    - **`[read-only]` escape for review and investigation.** Tasks that legitimately change no file carry `[read-only]` in their text (also `[read_only]` / `[read only]`) and complete freely. Because the marker is an annotation rather than part of identity, it can be appended to an already-planned task instead of forcing a re-plan. Every use is journaled as `todo_completed_read_only`, so relabeling real work as read-only is visible in the audit trail instead of passing silently. Deliberately dropped work uses `cancelled`.
    - **Planned late.** A task first observed already `completed` has no window, so it is scored against the session's mutation history, bounded by the one-mutation-per-completion rule.
    - **Block message names the remedy.** A rejected write names the offending tasks and states the three legitimate paths: do the work, mark it `[read-only]`, or mark it `cancelled`.
    - **Simulation predicts the gate.** `guard_why` now reports the same verdict the enforcement path would, and does not move any task window.
    - **Steering, not just enforcement.** The `todowrite` tool description, the system-prompt guidance, and the compaction injection now state the lifecycle contract: plan before working, keep the list truthful, complete a task only after its work is done, and use the marker for genuinely read-only tasks.
    - **`guard_status` reports `taskEvidence`** (`active`, `completed`, `tasksWithoutRecordedWork`, `readOnlyTasks`), so the requirement is visible before it blocks anything.

    Todo state is per session and cleared on `session.deleted`. The completion check never replaces the finalization gates: fresh verification evidence and the review gate remain the authority on whether the work is done.

- 2818ad0: Adopt five OpenCode 2 plugin APIs that were previously unused, and correct documentation that had drifted from the host.

    `ctx.command.transform` now registers a server-side `/guard-status` command, so guard state is readable from every V2 client without the separately installed TUI companion. The report is delivered as a synthetic message, which costs no model turn.

    Read-only subagent roles now lose the mutating tools from their per-request tool snapshot in `session.hook("context")` (`write`, `edit`, `patch`, `apply_patch`, `shell`, `bash`, `execute`, `todowrite`, `subagent`/`task`, and the worktree lifecycle tools). Previously they received guidance text and were denied late in `execute.before`; now the model cannot plan the call at all. The `execute.before` seat is unchanged and remains the backstop for tools supplied outside the host snapshot. Every pruning is journaled as `session.context` / `read_only_role_tools_pruned`.
